This is the source grant, not Kamal's software license. AGPL covers copyrightable works, not only binaries, and section5 expressly permits aggregation with independent works without relicensing those other works.
distribution_requirements: Retain the entire actual AGPL-3.0 license text with the dataset distribution, exact pinned source links, source project attribution and every applicable existing source copyright/license/no-warranty notice; do not fabricate a project copyright year or confuse FSF's copyright on the license text with authorship of PlaceCal.

Identify these three command-containing source excerpts per record as AGPL-3.0, not MIT or blanket permissive dataset content. Keep their preferred editable source form (existing JSONL/excerpts plus lineage) accessible alongside CSV; no object-code-only redistribution is proposed.

Mark dated extraction, removal of prose/comment prefixes and Russian annotation changes prominently. To the extent an annotated excerpt is a modified covered work, license that covered contribution as a whole under AGPL-3.0 and preserve downstream rights; do not restrict it via a dataset-wide EULA, no-redistribution clause or conflicting blanket license.

Treat unrelated independently sourced rows as a source collection/aggregate, not a linked executable or an extension of PlaceCal. The aggregate's compilation terms must not restrict rights granted for any included work; section5 does not automatically apply AGPL to unrelated records.

Section13's network-source condition concerns a modified covered program offered for remote interaction, not merely making an inert CSV download available. Do not claim it forces arbitrary unrelated dataset tooling/models to be AGPL or that it authorizes all conceivable downstream training/relicensing uses. Preserve source/license information for downstream assessment.
